Oct 25, 2026
95
DualShockers
Phantom Blade Zero is hands down the best action RPG this year, and quite honestly, one of the best action games I have played in a very long time. It has exceptional build variety, featuring an immense number of weapons and skills, all feeling distinct from each other and catering to different playstyles. It features a world filled with secrets, such as hidden bosses, storylines, and even completely optional regions, making exploration just as fantastic as its combat and progression systems. Despite its slight hiccups in performance, there's very little I'd change in S-Game's Phantom Blade Zero and I wouldn't be surprised if it ends up as a nominee for the grand prize at the Game Awards.

Gaming Boulevard
You can tell that Phantom Blade Zero is a passion project for the developers at S-GAME. Their love for Chinese folklore, environmental details and kung fu-style battles clearly shows. Even though the game has some similarities to Dark Souls, they have made all of these features their own and chosen a different path. The game looks and feels phenomenal, and even though some of the boss fights are challenging, the victories feel satisfying. The game encourages exploration and experimentation without all the suffering, and that makes it accessible enough to potentially become the “game of the year” for quite a few people.
PC FULL REVIEW
Oct 26, 2026
90
Adrenaline
Phantom Blade Zero delivers a surprisingly fresh and successful action experience, highlighted by its exceptional motion capture, dynamic combat, and 55 unique weapons. The game boasts stunning Unreal Engine 5 visuals and an immersive soundtrack. While the PC version suffers from optimization issues, particularly with Ray and Path Tracing enabled, these problems are not universal and can be mitigated. The narrative structure is somewhat confusing, but the core gameplay loop, deep upgrade systems, and challenging boss battles make it a standout. It successfully distances itself from the Soulslike genre, offering unrestricted, fast-paced hack-and-slash action.
PC FULL REVIEW

Gameliner
Phantom Blade Zero was absolutely worth the wait, delivering spectacular action, stunning visuals, and incredibly smooth, varied combat that makes wielding Soul’s sword an absolute blast. The boss fights offer a satisfying challenge, while the gorgeous world of Wulin oozes atmosphere, although its fairly linear levels and limited exploration leave a little to be desired. Still, with fantastic audio design, a great soundtrack, and excellent voice acting, Phantom Blade Zero is a must-play for anyone craving stylish action in a breathtaking Chinese setting.

GAMES.CH
Phantom Blade Zero delivers fast-paced combat, challenging boss encounters and stunning visuals in a world inspired by Chinese martial arts and mythology. Its extensive weapon selection, flexible progression system and reduced reliance on repetitive farming help it stand out from traditional Soulslikes. However, its relatively linear environments and occasionally overlong text passages hold it back. Fans of demanding action games and spectacular swordplay should find plenty to enjoy.

Oct 31, 2026
4
Kookaburra26
I also agree that a difficult game isn't necessarily a "Souls-like." But let’s be clear: The game was marketed as an Action-RPG adventure, and the marketing team explicitly stated that it would NOT have the same level of demands as games in the "Souls-like" genre. Naturally, players concluded that they wouldn't be facing "bullet-sponge" bosses (or rather, "HP-sponge" bosses) that unleash long combo chains, requiring precise parries and dodges with extremely punishing windows for counter-attacks.I acknowledge that there’s no respawn mechanic or loss of resources—fair enough. But look—if it takes you eight days (figuratively speaking) to take down a single boss, some people simply won't find that fun; had they known, they certainly wouldn't have bought the game. I understand that for those who enjoy this type of gameplay, the game might actually be too easy—but you also have to consider those for whom this is absolutely not their cup of tea. As I said, for me—and many others—this isn't at all the game I was expecting. There are several issues: the unacknowledged "Souls-lite" nature, the trailers that looked incredibly good... well, it *is* beautiful in places, but in others, it’s actually quite mediocre or even ugly. (I’m running it on a system with an RTX 5080, 64GB of RAM, and an i7 Ultra.) You might have a decent-looking panorama, but then you turn the camera and see rocks with low-resolution textures and jagged, poorly defined shapes. I’d love to get into the story (really! And i'm actually on the 3rd map), the lore, and the background, but honestly—it’s just poorly told! Crimson Desert was even better, and that wasn't even remotely the game's strong suit... Still, if some people are having fun, that’s great—honestly, I wish I could be like you and enjoy it, but... nope :'(
